DELUXE_ML_23_THE_GAP_UNDERGROUND = The Gap
DELUXE_ML_23_THE_GAP_UNDERGROUND_DESCRIPTION = Underground level of the Gap. This was one of the most challenging locations I designed for the game. We needed physical objects for interactions in The Gap where the player can select things like "Talents". These physical objects also needed to feel like they were a part of Dylan's subconsciousness. After a lot of sketching, expriments and reading about the subject I started coming up with some designs. I also got help from my colleague Michał Motulewicz who designed the "Artifacts" and "Training Arena" interactions. Concept by Markus Luotero

The Notice of Dispute sent by either party must include the sender’s name, address, and other contact information, a description of the Dispute (including any relevant account names), and what resolution to the Dispute is being sought.</p><p cohinline>The Informal Resolution requirement is designed to allow Remedy (or you, in the case of a Dispute Remedy asserts against you) to make a fair, fact-based offer of settlement if it chooses to do so. You or Remedy cannot proceed to arbitration before the end of the Informal Resolution period. If you or Remedy proceed to arbitration without providing a compliant Notice of Dispute and waiting until the conclusion of the Informal Resolution period, a court may enjoin the filing and order the party that has not followed the Informal Resolution process to reimburse the other party for any arbitration fees and costs already incurred. To the fullest extent allowed by applicable law, the arbitrator may not award money or other relief for the benefit of any person other than you or Remedy as part of the resolution of any Dispute.</p><p cohinline>“<b>Binding</b>” means that both you and Remedy will have to live with the arbitrator’s decision, except to the limited extent appeals to a court are permitted under the FAA. As limited by the FAA, this Agreement, and the Rules applicable to the arbitration, the arbitrator will have exclusive authority to make all procedural and substantive decisions regarding any Dispute and to grant any remedy that would otherwise be available in court, including the power to determine the question of arbitrability. The arbitrator will have authority to award temporary, interim, or permanent injunctive relief or relief providing for specific performance of this Agreement, but (as provided above) only to the extent necessary to provide relief to a party in arbitration warranted by the individual claim before the arbitrator. The award rendered by the arbitrator may be confirmed and enforced in any court having jurisdiction.</p><h4>Arbitration Procedure and Location</h4><p cohinline>You or Remedy may initiate arbitration of any Disputes not resolved by Informal Resolution by filing a Demand for Arbitration with JAMS in accordance with the Rules (or with AAA in accordance with the Rules if JAMS is not available to arbitrate the Dispute).</p><p cohinline>(Instructions for filing a Demand for Arbitration with JAMS are available on the JAMS website, and instructions for filing a Demand for Arbitration with AAA are available on the AAA website or by calling AAA at 800-778-7879.) You will send a copy of any Demand for Arbitration to Remedy Entertainment Plc, Legal Department, ATTN: ARBITRATION OF DISPUTE, Luomanportti 3, FI-02200 Espoo, Finland. Remedy will send any Demand for Arbitration to the e-mail address or other contact information you have provided to Remedy or that we have otherwise obtained.</p><p cohinline>The arbitration will be conducted by a single arbitrator. You and Remedy both agree that the arbitration will be conducted in the English language and that the arbitrator will be bound by this Agreement.</p><p cohinline>For Disputes in which the claimant seeks less than USD $10,000, the arbitrator will decide the matter solely on the basis of written submissions, without a formal hearing, unless the arbitrator decides that a formal hearing is necessary. For matters in which the claimant seeks USD $10,000 or more, or smaller matters in which the arbitrator determines a hearing to be necessary, hearings shall be conducted by video or telephone, unless the arbitrator determines an in-person hearing to be necessary. If an in-person hearing is required, the hearing will take place in New York County, New York, unless the arbitrator determines that this would pose a hardship for the claimant or that the claimant’s access to the arbitration would be precluded by such location, in which case the in-person hearing may be conducted in the claimant’s state.</p><p cohinline>The arbitrator (not a judge or jury) will resolve the Dispute. Unless you and Remedy agree otherwise, any decision or award will include a written statement stating the decision of each claim and the basis for the award, including the arbitrator’s essential factual and legal findings and conclusions.</p><p cohinline>To the fullest extent allowed by applicable law, the arbitrator may only award legal or equitable remedies that are individual to you or Remedy to satisfy one of our individual claims (that the arbitrator determines are supported by credible relevant evidence).</p><p cohinline>An arbitration award, and any judgment confirming it, applies only to that specific case; it cannot be used or offered as precedent in any other case except to enforce the award itself.</p><p cohinline>Any decision or award may be enforced as a final judgment by any court of competent jurisdiction or, if applicable, application may be made to such court for judicial confirmation of any award and an order of enforcement.</p><h4>Consumer Arbitration Fees</h4><p cohinline>If you start an arbitration against Remedy, you will pay the filing fee required for consumer arbitrations. Remedy or you may advise the other of its or your belief that cases are Coordinated Cases, and disputes over whether a case or cases meet the contractual definition of “<b>Coordinated Cases</b>” will be decided by the arbitration provider as an administrative matter. Demands for Arbitration in Coordinated Cases shall only be filed with the arbitration provider as permitted by the bellwether process set forth below. Remedy will pay only its share of arbitration fees for Coordinated Cases; the claimants will be responsible for their share of those fees. Applicable statutes of limitations will be tolled for claims asserted in a Coordinated Case from the time a compliant Notice of Dispute has been received by a party until, under the terms of this Agreement, the Coordinated Case may be filed in arbitration or court.</p><p cohinline>Once counsel in the Coordinated Cases has advised Remedy that all or substantially all of the Notices of Dispute have been provided, counsel for the parties shall confer in good faith regarding the number of cases that should proceed in arbitration as bellwethers, to allow each side to test the merits of its arguments. If counsel for the parties do not agree on the number of bellwethers, an even number shall be chosen by the arbitration provider as an administrative matter (or, in the arbitration provider’s discretion, by a process arbitrator). Factors that the arbitration provider may consider in making this decision include the complexity of the dispute and differences in facts or applicable laws among various cases. Once the number of bellwethers is fixed, by agreement or by the arbitration provider, each side shall select half that number from among the claimants who have provided compliant Notices of Dispute, and <b>only</b> those chosen cases may be filed with the arbitration provider. The parties acknowledge that resolution of some Coordinated Cases will be delayed by this bellwether process.</p><p cohinline>A single arbitrator shall preside over each Coordinated Case chosen for a bellwether proceeding, and only one Coordinated Case may be assigned to each arbitrator as part of a bellwether process unless the parties agree otherwise.</p><p cohinline>Once all bellwether trials have concluded (or sooner if the counsel for the claimants and Remedy agree), the parties must engage in a single mediation of all remaining Coordinated Cases, with each side paying half the applicable mediation fee. Remedy and counsel for the claimants must agree on a mediator within 30 days after the conclusion of the last bellwether trial. If counsel for Remedy and claimants cannot agree on a mediator within 30 days, the arbitration provider will appoint a mediator as an administrative matter. Remedy and counsel for the claimants will cooperate for the purpose of ensuring that the mediation is scheduled as quickly as practicable after the mediator is appointed.</p><p cohinline>If the mediation does not yield a global resolution, this arbitration requirement shall no longer apply to Disputes that are the subject of Coordinated Cases for which a compliant Notice of Dispute was received by the other party but that were not resolved in bellwether proceedings. Such Disputes may be filed only in the state courts in New York County, New York, or if federal jurisdiction exists, in the United States District Court for the Southern District of New York, and you consent as part of this Agreement to venue such cases exclusively in these courts. Nothing in this paragraph shall be construed as prohibiting either you or Remedy from removing a case from state to federal court if removal is allowed under applicable law. NARRATIVE_OBJECT_ENEMY_HEDRON_AGGREGATE_APEX_BODY = <strong>FIELD RESEARCH — HEDRON AGGREGATE (APEX SPECIMEN)</strong><br><strong>— CONFIDENTIAL / RESEARCH DIRECTORATE —</strong><br><br><strong>SUMMARY:</strong><br>An apex <strong>Aggregate</strong> specimen that, for most of an engagement, has proven resistant to direct harm. The entity hangs stationary in the air, sheathed in a protective resonance shield, and conducts the engagement at one remove — through a coordinated formation of attendant <strong>Flux</strong> units that orbit it as integral parts of its body. Recovered fragments include street hardware, sign metal, concrete, human material, and unidentified Astral Plane substrate arranged into a consistent mathematical order.<br><br><strong>OBSERVED BEHAVIOR:</strong><br>Attacks directed at the Aggregate itself are absorbed harmlessly by its shield. Trauma reaches the Aggregate only through the fluxes themselves: each Flux destroyed propagates a corresponding loss to the parent. Three recurring behavioral stages have been documented:<br>• Initial stage: the Aggregate fires geometric projectile patterns — rows, columns, diamonds — through gaps in the orbit. Horizontal and vertical fluxes execute spinning saw attacks in place, alternating.<br>• First structural break: the Aggregate falls dormant. Its fluxes detach and pursue the target as independent saws before returning.<br>• Escalated stage: behavior resumes with denser projectile patterns and faster flux rotation.<br>• Second structural break: fluxes are released a second time, but the Aggregate now <em>continues</em> to fire while they pursue.<br><br><strong>ASSESSMENT:</strong><br>An apex Aggregate is the clearest demonstration we have that a Hedron entity is not, in any meaningful sense, a single body. It is a <em>formation</em> — and dismantling it requires dismantling the formation, not the central node. The pattern is the organism. The pattern is also the weapon. We do not yet have a vocabulary for an entity whose vulnerability is distributed across its supporting cast, but we are going to need one.<br><br>Refer to file <i>■■■■</i> for full report.<br><br>—Dr. Emily Pope, Head of Research

NARRATIVE_OBJECT_ENEMY_HEDRON_AGGREGATE_BEAMS_APEX_BODY = <strong>FIELD RESEARCH — HEDRON AGGREGATE (BEAMS, APEX SPECIMEN)</strong><br><strong>— CONFIDENTIAL / RESEARCH DIRECTORATE —</strong><br><br><strong>SUMMARY:</strong><br>An apex <strong>Aggregate (Beams)</strong> specimen. The standing-shield architecture of the parent Apex is preserved, but the attached <strong>Flux</strong> units now function as ordered routing nodes: the Aggregate projects a beam onto a chosen Flux, which divides it into a family of secondary beams that converge on the target.<br><br><strong>OBSERVED BEHAVIOR:</strong><br>Three pairs of divided beams arrive in alternating sweeps. Three recurring stages have been documented:<br>• Initial stage: standard routed volleys at a measured cadence.<br>• First structural break: fluxes detach and patrol the surrounding space, firing paired beams in opposite directions — vertical fluxes upward and downward, horizontal fluxes laterally.<br>• Escalated stage: volley cadence increases markedly.<br>• Second structural break: fluxes resume independent patrol fire, and the Aggregate begins emitting horizontal and vertical <em>energy disks</em> in addition to its routed volleys.<br><br><strong>ASSESSMENT:</strong><br>The routing behavior is the most direct evidence yet that Hedron formations are coherent mathematical machines. Each Flux is not merely escorting the Aggregate; it is <em>participating</em> in the weapon. The bodies are assembled from found matter. The organization is anything but found.<br><br>Refer to file <i>■■■■</i> for full report.<br><br>—Dr. Emily Pope, Head of Research

NARRATIVE_OBJECT_ENEMY_HEDRON_AGGREGATE_WAVES_APEX_BODY = <strong>FIELD RESEARCH — HEDRON AGGREGATE (WAVES, APEX SPECIMEN)</strong><br><strong>— CONFIDENTIAL / RESEARCH DIRECTORATE —</strong><br><br><strong>SUMMARY:</strong><br>The "Waves" Aggregate is the only Hedron specimen we have cataloged that exists exclusively in its apex form. No baseline counterpart has ever been documented in the field. The entity hangs stationary in the air, fully shielded, and serves as a formation-source rather than a direct attacker — a role we previously associated only with the Hiss Blob.<br><br><strong>OBSERVED BEHAVIOR:</strong><br>The Aggregate Waves manifests supporting large-frame Hedron entities in four sequential waves, each assembled from available matter and organized into the same mathematical patterning as naturally encountered specimens. Each wave consists of two such entities and must be eliminated before the next wave manifests:<br>• <strong>Wave 1:</strong> two Aggregates.<br>• <strong>Wave 2:</strong> two Swarms.<br>• <strong>Wave 3:</strong> two Aggregate (Beams) specimens.<br>• <strong>Wave 4:</strong> two Swarm (Charging) specimens.<br>Throughout the engagement, ambient <strong>Flux</strong> units are continuously maintained around the Waves entity. Trauma to any manifested heavy propagates back to the Waves entity itself.<br><br><strong>ASSESSMENT:</strong><br>That this entity has no solo form is, by itself, the most interesting datum in the file. Every other Hedron specimen we have cataloged exists first as a discrete body and only secondarily participates in pattern dances. The Waves Aggregate is the inverse: it <em>is</em> the dance, with no underlying body to fall back on. If pattern is the medium of Hedron expression, then the Waves entity is what happens when the medium <em>writes its own author</em>. I am not entirely sure that sentence is overreach. I am working on it.<br><br>Refer to file <i>■■■■</i> for full report.<br><br>—Dr. Emily Pope, Head of Research

NARRATIVE_OBJECT_ENEMY_HEDRON_FLUX = Hedron Flux
NARRATIVE_OBJECT_ENEMY_HEDRON_FLUX_BODY = <strong>FIELD RESEARCH — HEDRON FLUX</strong><br><strong>— CONFIDENTIAL / RESEARCH DIRECTORATE —</strong><br><br><strong>SUMMARY:</strong><br>The smallest and most numerous documented expression of the <strong>Hedron</strong>-derived pattern entities. Flux units present as fragments of nearby material — road signage, parking-meter casings, broken concrete, occasional human tissue, and, in documented threshold-adjacent encounters, Astral Plane matter — arranged into a highly ordered mathematical pattern. When attacking, the pattern reshapes into vertical sawblades oriented perpendicular to the ground.<br><br><strong>OBSERVED BEHAVIOR:</strong><br>In isolation, the Flux is an aggressive short-range entity that crosses obstacles through rhythmic jumps and commits fully to close engagement. When accompanying a larger Hedron entity, however, its behavior alters entirely: it ceases acting as an independent combatant and integrates into a coordinated formation — a <strong>pattern dance</strong> — in which it functions as a disposable extension of the larger entity's movement.<br><br><strong>ASSESSMENT:</strong><br>The Flux is not, in any meaningful sense, a creature. It is a <em>note</em> in a longer composition we do not yet understand, written with whatever matter the pattern can reach. Whether that composition has an author — and by whom, and from where — is the central open question of all current Hedron research. Polaris suggested one form of paranatural intelligence. Hedron suggests another. I am increasingly convinced that what we are cataloging as individual "entities" is in fact the audible fraction of a much larger signal.<br><br>Refer to file <i>■■■■</i> for full report.<br><br>—Dr. Emily Pope, Head of Research

NARRATIVE_OBJECT_ENEMY_HEDRON_FLUX_HORIZONTAL_BODY = <strong>FIELD RESEARCH — HEDRON FLUX (HORIZONTAL VARIANT)</strong><br><strong>— CONFIDENTIAL / RESEARCH DIRECTORATE —</strong><br><br><strong>SUMMARY:</strong><br>A variant of the standard <strong>Flux</strong> that reshapes its local-material fragments into a sawblade pattern oriented parallel to the ground rather than perpendicular to it.<br><br><strong>OBSERVED BEHAVIOR:</strong><br>Behaviorally identical to the parent entity in all respects except attack orientation. Rather than pressing the target sideways, this variant presses the target upward: a jump, a surge, or any other means of leaving the ground plane.<br><br><strong>ASSESSMENT:</strong><br>Horizontal and vertical Flux units appear together in pattern dances with striking frequency. The two orientations together deny any single defensive response, compressing both ground and air into contested space at once. Whether that combination is emergent from the formation's internal logic, or externally authored somewhere upstream, is — as ever — the question we cannot yet resolve.<br><br>Refer to file <i>■■■■</i> for full report.<br><br>—Dr. Emily Pope, Head of Research

NARRATIVE_OBJECT_ENEMY_HEDRON_SWARM_APEX = Hedron Swarm — Apex
NARRATIVE_OBJECT_ENEMY_HEDRON_SWARM_APEX_BODY = <strong>FIELD RESEARCH — HEDRON SWARM (APEX SPECIMEN)</strong><br><strong>— CONFIDENTIAL / RESEARCH DIRECTORATE —</strong><br><br><strong>SUMMARY:</strong><br>An apex <strong>Swarm</strong> specimen. What the field encounters is not a single Swarm but a <em>cluster</em> of grouped Swarm bodies bound by a shared shield. Internally, the cluster organizes around a central <strong>Core</strong> surrounded by <strong>Satellite</strong> Swarms, all assembled from patterned local material.<br><br><strong>OBSERVED BEHAVIOR:</strong><br>Attacks directed at the cluster are absorbed by its shield. The Core is affected only when a Satellite has detached to act independently at range, mirroring the baseline Swarm's homing-projectile behavior. Trauma to a detached Satellite propagates to the Core. Three recurring stages have been documented:<br>• Initial stage: standard Satellite detach-and-fire cycle.<br>• First structural break: all Satellites recall to the Core; the Core manifests <strong>Flux</strong> units and seeds explosive proximity bodies around the target's position. During this interval, field teams report no reliable countermeasure beyond evasion.<br>• Escalated stage: resumed cycle, with shorter intervals between Satellite detachments.<br>• Second structural break: the explosive-seeding cadence increases and additional Fluxes are deployed.<br><br><strong>ASSESSMENT:</strong><br>The Apex Swarm is, structurally, an Aggregate inverted: a coalition of small bodies presenting as a single entity, rather than a single body presenting through a coalition of small ones. That the same faction produces both architectures is the most useful piece of information in this file. Hedron is not committed to a single organizational principle or a single material substrate. It is committed to whichever principle currently produces the strongest pattern. I am not sure we have ever met an opponent that was indifferent to its own form. I am sure I would prefer not to.<br><br>Refer to file <i>■■■■</i> for full report.<br><br>—Dr. Emily Pope, Head of Research

NARRATIVE_OBJECT_ENEMY_HEDRON_SWARM_BODY = <strong>FIELD RESEARCH — HEDRON SWARM</strong><br><strong>— CONFIDENTIAL / RESEARCH DIRECTORATE —</strong><br><br><strong>SUMMARY:</strong><br>A mid-frame airborne entity composed of the smallest discrete pattern fragments currently observable to the naked eye. The fragments are not a fixed substance. They are local matter organized into impossible order: signage, meters, asphalt, human material, and, in some documented instances, Astral Plane debris. Individually negligible. Collectively coherent: the fragments form a single cloud-like body with unified behavior and apparent intent.<br><br><strong>OBSERVED BEHAVIOR:</strong><br>The Swarm cruises at low altitude and never ascends beyond contact range. During engagement, it discharges sequential cloudlets at its target, each homing aggressively and detonating on contact. The parent mass remains in formation above, continuously regenerating its body from the surrounding pattern field.<br><br><strong>ASSESSMENT:</strong><br>The Swarm is a reminder that Hedron's organizational principle scales in both directions. A body composed of this many fragments implies, by the same logic, that a pattern considerably larger than the Swarm could exist — and that we have not yet encountered it. Or have not yet recognized it when we did. The material is incidental. The arrangement is the entity.<br><br>Refer to file <i>■■■■</i> for full report.<br><br>—Dr. Emily Pope, Head of Research

The implications, if borne out, extend well beyond this specimen profile. I have requested a comparative analysis with the gravitic anomalies cataloged during the original Oldest House incident. I expect the comparison to be uncomfortable.<br><br>Refer to file <i>■■■■</i> for full report.<br><br>—Dr. Emily Pope, Head of Research

The opinion is not unanimous within the directorate.<br><br>Refer to file <i>■■■■</i> for full report.<br><br>—Dr. Emily Pope, Head of Research

NARRATIVE_OBJECT_ENEMY_HISS_BLOB_APEX_BODY = <strong>FIELD RESEARCH — HISS BLOB (APEX SPECIMEN)</strong><br><strong>— CONFIDENTIAL / RESEARCH DIRECTORATE —</strong><br><br><strong>SUMMARY:</strong><br>An advanced <strong>Blob</strong> specimen retaining the same corrupted-bus origin as the baseline profile. The Apex has acquired an unsettling new behavior: rather than simply releasing <strong>Mini-Blobs</strong> into its vicinity, it <em>launches</em> them at the target as ballistic projectiles.<br><br><strong>OBSERVED BEHAVIOR:</strong><br>When the target is in line of sight, the Blob fires Mini-Blobs in straight trajectories as a multi-shot volley. Each impact produces a localized blast, after which any surviving passenger-seat fragment continues to behave as an independent minor entity. Only some released or launched Mini-Blobs have been observed detonating on death; affected fragments show a distinct resonance instability at the moment they leave the parent body. Three exposed passenger clusters are present along the bus windows; rupturing them produces a convulsion throughout the whole body.<br><br><strong>ASSESSMENT:</strong><br>The Apex Blob does not treat the passengers it releases as survivors, or even as remains. It treats them as <em>ammunition</em>, but not uniformly. Some passenger-seat fragments are expelled as mobile bodies. Others are made volatile first, carrying the parent body's resonance instability with them until death releases it. The window clusters make the reading difficult to avoid: bodies caught in the act of trying to escape, preserved as part of the structure, then used as the structure's most vulnerable points. The Apex Blob is the same Hiss logic applied to an entire vehicle full of people, one passenger at a time.<br><br>Refer to file <i>■■■■</i> for full report.<br><br>—Dr. Emily Pope, Head of Research

NARRATIVE_OBJECT_ENEMY_HISS_BLOB_BODY = <strong>FIELD RESEARCH — HISS BLOB</strong><br><strong>— CONFIDENTIAL / RESEARCH DIRECTORATE —</strong><br><br><strong>SUMMARY:</strong><br>A Hiss-corrupted city bus filled with passengers, now fused into a single mobile mass. Field teams labeled the first specimen <em>"the bus"</em> before realizing the description was not figurative. It appears to be the primary source of <strong>Mini-Blob</strong> entities: passengers fused with the bus seats that held them during the corruption event.<br><br><strong>OBSERVED BEHAVIOR:</strong><br>The Blob avoids sustained direct engagement. When these clusters are ruptured, the whole structure convulses.<br><br><strong>ASSESSMENT:</strong><br>Teleportation on this scale has never been observed in the Oldest House record for any Hiss entity. This relocation appears to be unique to the Blob among documented Hiss specimens — yet the more immediate horror is simpler than the physics. This was public transportation. A closed vehicle full of people with nowhere to go when the resonance reached them. The Hiss did not make a monster shaped like a bus. It kept the bus, and everyone inside it, and taught the result to move.<br><br>Refer to file <i>■■■■</i> for full report.<br><br>—Dr. Emily Pope, Head of Research

Given the current outbreak's access to a densely populated urban corridor, this economy of disposability is not likely to improve on its own.<br><br>Refer to file <i>■■■■</i> for full report.<br><br>—Dr. Emily Pope, Head of Research

NARRATIVE_OBJECT_ENEMY_HISS_DISTORTED_APEX_BODY = <strong>FIELD RESEARCH — HISS DISTORTED (APEX SPECIMEN)</strong><br><strong>— CONFIDENTIAL / RESEARCH DIRECTORATE —</strong><br><br><strong>SUMMARY:</strong><br>An advanced <strong>Distorted</strong> specimen exhibiting the same core behaviors as the baseline profile at significantly greater intensity: faster concealment, shorter intervals between attacks, and a markedly wider and longer forward concussive cone.<br><br><strong>OBSERVED BEHAVIOR:</strong><br>The signature cone manifests at substantially greater range and with less recovery time between manifestations. I have asked Operations to treat all Distorted sightings as potential Apex contacts until visual confirmation proves otherwise.<br><br>Refer to file <i>■■■■</i> for full report.<br><br>—Dr. Emily Pope, Head of Research
NARRATIVE_OBJECT_ENEMY_HISS_DISTORTED_APEX_COLLECTED = <b>Hiss Distorted — Apex</b> research collected

NARRATIVE_OBJECT_ENEMY_HISS_DISTORTED_BODY = <strong>FIELD RESEARCH — HISS DISTORTED</strong><br><strong>— CONFIDENTIAL / RESEARCH DIRECTORATE —</strong><br><br><strong>SUMMARY:</strong><br>A large-frame entity that retains the <em>paranatural invisibility</em> first cataloged during the original Oldest House incident. The Distorted stalks its target in full concealment, emerging only at close range to release a short concussive wave in a forward cone before vanishing again.<br><br><strong>OBSERVED BEHAVIOR:</strong><br>The cone is preceded by a visible gathering period, and the Distorted is stationary during its execution. The attack itself is rarely what proves lethal. The <em>pursuit</em> is. The entity favors corridors, narrow streets, flooded subway platforms, stairwells — any environment in which sightlines break quickly and escape paths are limited.<br><br><strong>ASSESSMENT:</strong><br>The Distorted's invisibility remains our <em>least</em> understood Hiss capability. Years of encounters. Dozens of recovered fragments. We still do not know whether the entity is bending light, bending the witness's perception, or both simultaneously. If anyone reading this report has direct observational footage of a Distorted mid-attack, please forward it to the Research directorate. Any frame count. Any fidelity. I am serious.<br><br>Refer to file <i>■■■■</i> for full report.<br><br>—Dr. Emily Pope, Head of Research

NARRATIVE_OBJECT_ENEMY_MOLD_MOLDBAG = Moldbag
NARRATIVE_OBJECT_ENEMY_MOLD_MOLDBAG_BODY = <strong>FIELD RESEARCH — MOLDBAG</strong><br><strong>— CONFIDENTIAL / RESEARCH DIRECTORATE —</strong><br><br><strong>SUMMARY:</strong><br>The most common Mold-infected host documented in the current outbreak. Each specimen consists of a human body protruding from a larger ambulatory Mold mass, the remaining anatomy swallowed by fungal tissue. Unlike Hiss manifestations, the Moldbag does <em>not</em> attack on sight — it will tolerate an uncorrupted observer indefinitely until provoked or approached too closely.<br><br><strong>OBSERVED BEHAVIOR:</strong><br>When engaged, Moldbags pursue slowly and deliberately. On sustaining damage — or when a target closes into proximity — the host expels a lingering cloud of Mold spores that contaminates the immediate area. Multiple simultaneous discharges can render a small area unbreathable for a significant duration. Visible facial expression, where preserved, has been consistently placid. Several Rangers described the hosts as smiling. Thermal exposure rapidly blackens exposed Mold tissue; blunt impact is absorbed by the soft mass with limited effect, and Mold-derived spores, pools, and contaminated ground produce no measurable injury to the organism.<br><br><strong>ASSESSMENT:</strong><br>The Mold's passivity should not be mistaken for restraint. The organism is simply unhurried. The serenity of the absorbed host complicates the picture in ways I do not like. Pain response is absent, distress is absent, and the exposed human portion presents as content to belong to the larger organism. Whether that contentment is chemically induced, neurologically imposed, or only an expression left behind by dead tissue is still under review. None of those options are comforting.<br><br>Refer to file <i>■■■■</i> for full report.<br><br>—Dr. Emily Pope, Head of Research

NARRATIVE_OBJECT_ENEMY_MOLD_MOLDBAG_ROCKET = Moldbag (Launcher)
NARRATIVE_OBJECT_ENEMY_MOLD_MOLDBAG_ROCKET_BODY = <strong>FIELD RESEARCH — MOLDBAG (LAUNCHER VARIANT)</strong><br><strong>— CONFIDENTIAL / RESEARCH DIRECTORATE —</strong><br><br><strong>SUMMARY:</strong><br>A variant of the standard <strong>Moldbag</strong> whose human component protrudes from the fungal mass without arms. Where the head should be, the Mold has opened a crude launch cavity rimmed with wet fungal tissue. The entity fires single-shot explosive spore clusters at medium range rather than closing distance. Baseline behavior is otherwise identical to the parent profile.<br><br><strong>OBSERVED BEHAVIOR:</strong><br>Projectiles travel on a lazy, readable arc. Groups positioned on elevated ground sustain coordinated saturation fire. As with all Mold manifestations, the entity does not initiate engagement until provoked — and does not cease it once it has begun. The exposed torso retains the same serene posture documented in baseline Moldbags, despite the absence of head and arms. Heat quickly destabilizes the launch cavity and surrounding tissue; blunt force is poorly transmitted through the soft mass, and Mold contamination has no observable effect on the entity.<br><br><strong>ASSESSMENT:</strong><br>The Mold's tendency to reshape host anatomy toward <em>specific</em> weapon roles is becoming increasingly difficult to attribute to generic corruption. This is tailoring. The Launcher is particularly blunt evidence: the organism has removed the parts of the person it does not need and opened a firing organ where identity used to be. The remaining body still presents as calm. I have hypotheses. I have no conclusions I am happy to write down.<br><br>Refer to file <i>■■■■</i> for full report.<br><br>—Dr. Emily Pope, Head of Research

NARRATIVE_OBJECT_ENEMY_MOLD_MOLDBAG_SHOTGUN = Moldbag (Scatter)
NARRATIVE_OBJECT_ENEMY_MOLD_MOLDBAG_SHOTGUN_BODY = <strong>FIELD RESEARCH — MOLDBAG (SCATTER VARIANT)</strong><br><strong>— CONFIDENTIAL / RESEARCH DIRECTORATE —</strong><br><br><strong>SUMMARY:</strong><br>A heavier variant of the <strong>Moldbag</strong> whose protruding human component has been reinforced with chitinous plating and a wide-dispersal spore organ. Rather than closing distance, this variant discharges a spreading burst of projectiles that explode on impact and leave a short-lived Mold-contaminated patch at each impact point.<br><br><strong>OBSERVED BEHAVIOR:</strong><br>Slow rate of discharge; devastating at short-to-medium distance. A single Scatter Moldbag substantially alters the usable geometry of a tight corridor. Multiple specimens underground produce stacked, long-persisting contaminated patches. Heavy blunt impacts break the chitinous reinforcement most reliably; once exposed, the soft Mold tissue absorbs blunt force but blackens rapidly under fire. Its own contaminated patches have produced no injury to the entity. Preserved faces show the same blissful affect as the parent profile.<br><br><strong>ASSESSMENT:</strong><br>The Scatter variant clarifies an emerging specialization pattern: the Mold is not producing uniform hosts with minor variation. It is producing role-optimized forms from a shared set of biological components. Plating for some, launch anatomy for others, substrate control for a third class — each tailored to a distinct field role. The host's apparent happiness may not be incidental to that process. Consent is too strong a word. Invitation may not be strong enough.<br><br>Refer to file <i>■■■■</i> for full report.<br><br>—Dr. Emily Pope, Head of Research

NARRATIVE_OBJECT_ENEMY_MOLD_PLAGUE = Mold Plague
NARRATIVE_OBJECT_ENEMY_MOLD_PLAGUE_APEX = Mold Plague — Apex
NARRATIVE_OBJECT_ENEMY_MOLD_PLAGUE_APEX_BODY = <strong>FIELD RESEARCH — MOLD PLAGUE (APEX SPECIMEN)</strong><br><strong>— CONFIDENTIAL / RESEARCH DIRECTORATE —</strong><br><br><strong>SUMMARY:</strong><br>A massively engorged <strong>Plague</strong> specimen with multiple human bodies protruding from the fungal mass. Volley cadence from the head-mouth opening is significantly elevated, but the more important development concerns its short-range downward expulsion: the resulting fungal pool no longer functions as contamination alone. It now functions as a generative site.<br><br><strong>OBSERVED BEHAVIOR:</strong><br>Projectile discharge from the head-mouth opening occurs at a substantially shorter interval than baseline. The downward expulsion deposits a persistent Mold zone around the entity from which, after a short delay, <em>new Mold bodies emerge fully formed</em>. Specimens observed include smaller-frame Moldbags and, in one verified incident, a juvenile Spitter. The mouth structure remains the primary discharge organ. The protruding hosts appear serene throughout the process. The engorged body resists blunt impacts by yielding around them, but sustained fire collapses exposed tissue; Mold pools and other Mold-origin contamination produce no injury.<br><br><strong>ASSESSMENT:</strong><br>The Plague was already classed as a siege engine. The Apex variant is something closer to a portable foundry. Reshaping terrain into Mold substrate was, in our previous analysis, a strategic prelude to colonization. We can now see that the same substrate is also being used as a manufacturing medium — that is, the terrain is being prepared not only to be <em>held</em> but to be <em>populated</em>, on demand, by the same engagement that produced it. The serene human expressions make the process feel less like construction and more like recruitment. The implications for any forward containment line are considerable.<br><br>Refer to file <i>■■■■</i> for full report.<br><br>—Dr. Emily Pope, Head of Research

NARRATIVE_OBJECT_ENEMY_MOLD_PLAGUE_BARRAGE = Mold Plague (Barrage)
NARRATIVE_OBJECT_ENEMY_MOLD_PLAGUE_BARRAGE_BODY = <strong>FIELD RESEARCH — MOLD PLAGUE (BARRAGE VARIANT)</strong><br><strong>— CONFIDENTIAL / RESEARCH DIRECTORATE —</strong><br><br><strong>SUMMARY:</strong><br>A variation of the <strong>Mold Plague</strong> whose dorsal surface has sprouted several mortar-like launch tubes around the human bodies protruding from the shared mass. These fire high-arcing projectiles <em>straight up</em> into the air, where they expand into large inert "cotton ball" mines that detonate on proximity — or eventually on their own, if undisturbed.<br><br><strong>OBSERVED BEHAVIOR:</strong><br>The Barrage Plague effectively plants a three-dimensional minefield <em>above</em> the surrounding space. The launch tubes themselves function as exposed growths; catastrophic damage to any tube produces a localized explosion, briefly collapses the entity's cohesion, and permanently reduces its rate of discharge. In enclosed environments, the entity falls back to a low-arc fire pattern that is significantly less expansive. Fire exposure remains highly effective against exposed tissue; blunt impacts sink into the mass, and Mold-produced mines or pools do not harm the organism.<br><br><strong>ASSESSMENT:</strong><br>Whatever process produced the Barrage Plague appears to have been tuned for open airspace. That the entity is measurably less effective indoors suggests that its origin — organism, external intelligence, or otherwise — did not anticipate confined conditions. The Mold rarely concedes a design limitation. When it does, the admission is worth noting. The exposed hosts, meanwhile, appear as serenely joined to the body as those in the parent profile.<br><br>Refer to file <i>■■■■</i> for full report.<br><br>—Dr. Emily Pope, Head of Research

NARRATIVE_OBJECT_ENEMY_MOLD_PLAGUE_BODY = <strong>FIELD RESEARCH — MOLD PLAGUE</strong><br><strong>— CONFIDENTIAL / RESEARCH DIRECTORATE —</strong><br><br><strong>SUMMARY:</strong><br>A large-frame Mold entity built from a grossly engorged fungal mass with multiple human bodies protruding from its surface. The Plague is slow and deliberate, reshaping the surrounding terrain as it advances.<br><br><strong>OBSERVED BEHAVIOR:</strong><br>The Plague fires arcing grenade-like projectiles from a swollen head-mouth opening; the projectiles detonate on impact and deposit persistent fungal pools across the terrain. At close range, the same opening discharges a short-range downward expulsion. Trauma to the mouth structure measurably reduces the entity's rate of discharge. Thermal exposure remains the most consistent way to collapse exposed Plague tissue; blunt impacts are absorbed by the engorged mass, and Mold pools or spore contamination do not injure it. The exposed hosts show no visible distress. If anything, their expressions suggest relief.<br><br><strong>ASSESSMENT:</strong><br>The Plague's attack profile is not primarily about damaging its target in a single exchange. It is about <em>reshaping the ground</em>. Every successful volley converts unclaimed terrain into claimed fungal substrate, usable by the Mold as a whole. The human components appear equally claimed: not merely trapped in the organism, but incorporated into it with an expression of impossible satisfaction. That may be the Mold's most effective camouflage. Not the spores. The invitation.<br><br>Refer to file <i>■■■■</i> for full report.<br><br>—Dr. Emily Pope, Head of Research

NARRATIVE_OBJECT_ENEMY_MOLD_SPITTER = Mold Spitter
NARRATIVE_OBJECT_ENEMY_MOLD_SPITTER_BODY = <strong>FIELD RESEARCH — MOLD SPITTER</strong><br><strong>— CONFIDENTIAL / RESEARCH DIRECTORATE —</strong><br><br><strong>SUMMARY:</strong><br>A stationary Mold host that has anchored itself to the substrate and grown into a rapid-fire spore-projector. Like all Mold manifestations, it is passive until attacked — and, like all Mold manifestations, that passivity is conditional.<br><br><strong>OBSERVED BEHAVIOR:</strong><br>Once engaged, the Spitter produces a dense volley of high-velocity spore projectiles in a sustained stream. The entity does not walk. Once per engagement, it retracts into the Mold substrate beneath it and grows back up at a distance, already rooted in the new position. Upon death the body ruptures, leaving behind a persistent Mold contamination. Fire exposure collapses Spitter tissue quickly; blunt impacts tend to compress rather than rupture the soft body, and active Mold contamination has no observable effect on the entity.<br><br><strong>ASSESSMENT:</strong><br>The Spitter's single-use regrowth is not documented in any Hiss entity. It is Mold-specific, and consistent with the colonial, networked nature of the organism. The fungal mass filling the walls of an infected building may, from the Mold's perspective, be indistinguishable from the host's own body. That raises the uncomfortable question of what counts as the Spitter's <em>location</em> at any given moment — and, by extension, how many "Spitters" may in fact be a single organism sampling itself at different coordinates.<br><br>Refer to file <i>■■■■</i> for full report.<br><br>—Dr. Emily Pope, Head of Research

NARRATIVE_OBJECT_ENEMY_MOLD_SPORE = Mold Spore
NARRATIVE_OBJECT_ENEMY_MOLD_SPORE_BODY = <strong>FIELD RESEARCH — MOLD SPORE</strong><br><strong>— CONFIDENTIAL / RESEARCH DIRECTORATE —</strong><br><br><strong>SUMMARY:</strong><br>A mid-frame airborne entity. The Spore presents as a floating sac — a colony body enclosing an unknown number of partially absorbed smaller hosts. Emitter points distributed across its outer surface allow the entity to discharge projectiles in any direction without reorienting its body.<br><br><strong>OBSERVED BEHAVIOR:</strong><br>The Spore drifts slowly and never ascends beyond the reach of a standard paranatural jump. When the target is within effective range, it unleashes sustained volleys from multiple emitters simultaneously, producing a crossfire from a single point. The sac's soft tissue deforms around blunt impacts, but blackens and fails rapidly under sustained fire. Mold-origin spores and contaminated zones have not produced injury in any observed Spore specimen.<br><br><strong>ASSESSMENT:</strong><br>Dissection of neutralized Spore bodies confirms what long-distance observation had already suggested: there <em>are</em> people inside. Or, more precisely, there <em>were</em>. Whether the occupants retained any discernible cortical activity at the time of final absorption is currently under review. Samples pending. I am not looking forward to the results.<br><br>Refer to file <i>■■■■</i> for full report.<br><br>—Dr. Emily Pope, Head of Research

NARRATIVE_OBJECT_ENEMY_MOLD_SPORE_MINES = Mold Spore (Mines)
NARRATIVE_OBJECT_ENEMY_MOLD_SPORE_MINES_BODY = <strong>FIELD RESEARCH — MOLD SPORE (MINE VARIANT)</strong><br><strong>— CONFIDENTIAL / RESEARCH DIRECTORATE —</strong><br><br><strong>SUMMARY:</strong><br>A variant of the standard <strong>Mold Spore</strong> that is visually bulkier, heavily armored, and specialized for sustained terrain contamination rather than direct assault.<br><br><strong>OBSERVED BEHAVIOR:</strong><br>Rather than firing at its target, the Mine variant drifts slowly and deposits proximity-triggered spore pods across the ground beneath it. Over the course of a prolonged engagement, the floor accumulates enough of these pods to make movement through the area difficult. The pods can be detonated before contact. Blunt impacts break the outer armor more reliably than precision cutting; only after that armor is fully destroyed does the soft sac beneath become reachable. Once exposed, the sac absorbs blunt force and is far more vulnerable to fire. The deposited pods and their contamination do not injure Mold tissue.<br><br><strong>ASSESSMENT:</strong><br>The Mine Spore is the clearest example yet of the Mold's preference for <em>environmental</em> rather than punctual warfare. The organism appears to have no concept of an engagement that ends. Every fight is a seeding opportunity. The mines are not simply weapons — they are intended to remain in place after the immediate encounter has resolved, extending the Mold's influence through time as well as through space.<br><br>Refer to file <i>■■■■</i> for full report.<br><br>—Dr. Emily Pope, Head of Research

International Data Transfers</h3><p cohinline>Our Services are global by nature and your data may therefore be transferred internationally. Since data protection laws vary by country, we implement various safeguards to protect your data. These may include EU-approved standard contractual clauses and other legal protections.</p><h3>6. Your Rights</h3><p cohinline>As a data subject, you have the right to:</p><ul><li>Access your Personal Data and receive a copy of the Personal Data you have provided to us.</li><li>Request that your Personal Data be transmitted from one system to another if the data has been provided by you and if the processing of the Personal Data is based on your consent or a contract, when technically feasible.</li><li>Request that we correct or erase (the right to be forgotten) your Personal Data.</li><li>Request that we restrict the processing of your Personal Data.</li><li>Object to the processing of your Personal Data if it is based on our legitimate interest.</li><li>Withdraw your consent where you have provided it.</li><li>Non-discrimination: We will not discriminate against you for exercising any of your rights hereunder.</li></ul><p cohinline>Requests about your Personal Data should be addressed to privacy@remedygames.com. When making a request, please provide sufficient information to allow us to locate and deliver the requested data and to verify your identity. If you request multiple copies of your Personal Data, make repeated requests, or if your request is deemed manifestly unfounded or excessive, we may charge a small fee to cover administrative costs.</p><p cohinline>If you are dissatisfied with how we handle your Personal Data, you may also file a complaint with us. If you feel that your complaint has not been adequately addressed, you may contact the relevant supervisory authority.</p><h3>7. Children</h3><p cohinline>Our Services are generally not directed to children under 16 (or other age as required by applicable local law). If you are a parent or guardian concerned about the transfer of your child’s Personal Data, please contact us.</p><h3>8. Changes to this Policy</h3><p cohinline>We reserve the right to change this Policy at any time by posting a modified version online at www.remedygames.com and our other websites, so please review it frequently to ensure you are aware of any changes.</p>

SWARM_DESCRIPTION = A threat assessment document on the Hedron Sequence.
SWARM_MELEE_DESCRIPTION = A threat assessment document on the Hedron Vector.
SWARM_MELEE_NAME = Hedron Vector
SWARM_MELEE_TRANSCRIPT = <b>THREAT ASSESSMENT: HEDRON VECTOR</b><br><br>- Classification: Heavy<br>- Visually resembles a brick wall pulled together into a toroid-like shape<br>- Flight-capable in a way bricks really aren’t supposed to be; charges rapidly at threats<br>- Releases a wave of “force” (field reports are as of yet inconclusive; tentatively a wave of kinetic energy?) at the end of the charge<br>- After performing the charge, the Hedron Vector becomes immobile (resting? recharging?)<br>- This passive state is short-lived, but does render the Hedron Vector vulnerable<br>- (For anyone unfortunate enough to end up fighting one of these things, I hereby officially endorse a “kick ‘em while they’re down” policy; you’re welcome)<br><br>Lydia M.B. McPierce<br>Senior Analyst, Threat Assessment Team
SWARM_NAME = Hedron Sequence
SWARM_TRANSCRIPT = <b>THREAT ASSESSMENT: HEDRON SEQUENCE</b><br><br>- Classification: Heavy<br>- Presents as a torus-shaped “swarm” of objects<br>- Maneuverable, defies gravity, attempts to maintain visual contact with threats<br>- (“Visual contact” is somewhat misleading given that they have no eyes and we have no idea how they sense anything – “line of sight” would probably be more accurate, but it’s not like we even know that they have sight, so... ignore me)<br>- Fires medium-speed projectiles in groups of three<br>- Projectiles aren’t ballistic; rather, they pursue targets<br>- Speculation: given the self-targeting/gravity-defying nature of the projectiles, is it possible they are actually appendage-like parts of the torus despite their (apparent?) physical separation from the Hedron Sequence?<br>If so, then the Hedron Sequence isn’t “firing” anything, it’s reaching out to touch targets<br>- (...very creepy)<br><br>Lydia M.B. McPierce<br>Senior Analyst, Threat Assessment Team
